55d4eca7-c873-450f-8b1e-318aa21f3744.canto_summary:
Having stayed overnight at Visala as an honoured guest of Sumati, Sri Rama,
accompanied by Viswamitra and the other sages, heads towards Mithila
(the capital of King Janaka) and, on reaching on the way a deserted
hermitage and, inquiring about it, is told by Viswamitra how
Ahalya, wife of Sage Gautama, whose hermitage it was,
was subjected to a curse by her husband

4c4e5d14-6edf-44ff-a28c-48e052b16360.canto_summary:
Having stayed overnight at Visala as an honoured guest of Sumati, Sri Rama,
accompanied by Viswamitra and the other sages, heads towards Mithila
(the capital of King Janaka) and, on reaching on the way a deserted
hermitage and, inquiring about it, is told by Viswamitra how
Ahalya, wife of Sage Gautama, whose hermitage it was,
was subjected to a curse by her husband

a8651939-6665-491a-b59e-314d336bbb12.canto_summary:
At the intercession of the gods, Indra is supplied with testicles of a ram;
Ahalya gets back her pristine celestial form at the very sight of
Sri Rama, the moment he enters the hermitage, and the two
divine brothers are entertained by the lady
with the help of her husband

58be0c6c-5cd5-4049-b43c-760e03479bea.canto_summary:
At the intercession of the gods, Indra is supplied with testicles of a ram;
Ahalya gets back her pristine celestial form at the very sight of
Sri Rama, the moment he enters the hermitage, and the two
divine brothers are entertained by the lady
with the help of her husband

b97a420c-f979-4d90-9607-8f96cae2eb24.canto_summary:
Sri Rama and others reach Mithila and are received in advance by
King Janaka, headed by his family priest, Satananda; Viswamitra
satisfies their curiosity about the two princes of Ayodhya

a16ae9d4-8e7a-4eca-a75a-1db9261263e3.canto_summary:
Sri Rama and others reach Mithila and are received in advance by
King Janaka, headed by his family priest, Satananda; Viswamitra
satisfies their curiosity about the two princes of Ayodhya

81cbe160-83c3-406a-855b-6fe15a55160f.canto_summary:
At the request of Satananda, Viswamitra tells him how Ahalya was redeemed
by Sri Rama and entertained him with the help of her husband. And Satananda
in his turn commences narrating to Sri Rama the story of Viswamitra

67ea3cf1-8763-475c-9ff2-2d3d01d2b48e.canto_summary:
At the request of Satananda, Viswamitra tells him how Ahalya was redeemed
by Sri Rama and entertained him with the help of her husband. And Satananda
in his turn commences narrating to Sri Rama the story of Viswamitra

1803c3d4-404d-434b-99fb-d39bd715ae61.canto_summary:
Vasistha enjoins his cow of plenty, Sabala by name, to yield
necessary articles for entertaining Viswamitra

256436d0-ee27-4650-89a0-b49654f67896.canto_summary:
Vasistha enjoins his cow of plenty, Sabala by name, to yield
necessary articles for entertaining Viswamitra

8f29155d-051f-403d-aa23-2a37aee53d0f.canto_summary:
Heartily entertained alongwith his army by Vasistha with delicious foods and
drinks yielded by his cow of plenty, Viswamitra asks of him the cow,
which Vasistha declines to part with

bf9d74b4-b913-4a80-a476-35b08704d17b.canto_summary:
Heartily entertained alongwith his army by Vasistha with delicious foods and
drinks yielded by his cow of plenty, Viswamitra asks of him the cow,
which Vasistha declines to part with

f3108f1e-d5e7-46ef-9fbb-ffbc5540a20e.canto_summary:
On Viswamitra attempting to take her away by force, Sabala seeks to know
Vasistha’s mind, and at his instance produces a multitude of warriors
that disperse ViSwamitra’s army

f9a4b80a-a394-49ec-b572-b9fffd3391cd.canto_summary:
On Viswamitra attempting to take her away by force, Sabala seeks to know
Vasistha’s mind, and at his instance produces a multitude of warriors
that disperse ViSwamitra’s army

83f6ea1b-f986-4eb9-97d5-339f1842bc94.canto_summary:
His entire army having been exterminated by the warriors produced by Sabala
and his hundred sons reduced to ashes by the very roar of Vasistha
even as they assailed him, Viswamitra retires to the Himalayas
for austerities and, receiving a number of missiles from
Lord Siva, tries them on the inmates of Vasistha’s
hermitage; Vasistha meets him with a mere staff
appropriate to a Brahmana

3d564658-4cf8-4448-ba39-22686dda41e0.canto_summary:
His entire army having been exterminated by the warriors produced by Sabala
and his hundred sons reduced to ashes by the very roar of Vasistha
even as they assailed him, Viswamitra retires to the Himalayas
for austerities and, receiving a number of missiles from
Lord Siva, tries them on the inmates of Vasistha’s
hermitage; Vasistha meets him with a mere staff
appropriate to a Brahmana

66f1f495-3c92-4b99-816d-7b2c90cd6a7c.canto_summary:
With his Brahmanical staff alone Vasistha renders ineffectual all the mystic
missiles discharged by ViSwamitra, whereupon the latter condemns

military strength and makes up his mind to practise austerities
with a view to attaining Brahmanhood

6be08e5d-7bd7-45b8-995a-4d19faf3e22e.canto_summary:
With his Brahmanical staff alone Vasistha renders ineffectual all the mystic
missiles discharged by ViSwamitra, whereupon the latter condemns

military strength and makes up his mind to practise austerities
with a view to attaining Brahmanhood

160adc76-6832-436d-ba76-836bb763430e.canto_summary:
Viswamitra embarks on a severe course of austerities with a view
to attaining Brahmanhood. In the meantime, King TriSanku of
Ayodhya requests Vasistha to conduct for him a sacrifice
which may enable him bodily to ascend to heaven and,
on Vasistha declining to comply with his request,
approaches his sons for the same purpose

7b140bcf-ae95-4b4c-b416-5e35dc9cfd25.canto_summary:
Viswamitra embarks on a severe course of austerities with a view
to attaining Brahmanhood. In the meantime, King TriSanku of
Ayodhya requests Vasistha to conduct for him a sacrifice
which may enable him bodily to ascend to heaven and,
on Vasistha declining to comply with his request,
approaches his sons for the same purpose

40ca2c44-1f54-4da3-a42a-c9121daa4edd.canto_summary:
Having been repulsed by Vasistha’s sons as well, Trisanku gets ready
to seek another priest, whereupon he is degraded by the curse of
Vasistha’s sons to the position of a Candala and approaches
Viswamitra with the same request

81ed5463-db8f-4439-9eb3-f76755b1b5d2.canto_summary:
Having been repulsed by Vasistha’s sons as well, Trisanku gets ready
to seek another priest, whereupon he is degraded by the curse of
Vasistha’s sons to the position of a Candala and approaches
Viswamitra with the same request

3c1ca9bb-ef1e-4c4b-b7e2-1aea0a96e3ac.canto_summary:
Viswamitra assures TriSanku of his help, sends word to a number of sages,
inviting them to conduct a sacrifice for Trisanku, and pronounces
a curse on those who decline to come

c240a5af-1ffd-4946-b9c4-c312a72b2488.canto_summary:
Viswamitra assures TriSanku of his help, sends word to a number of sages,
inviting them to conduct a sacrifice for Trisanku, and pronounces
a curse on those who decline to come

ae771cab-2fde-49bf-9ae0-50ea0138c198.canto_summary:
Viswamitra assures TriSanku of his help, sends word to a number of sages,
inviting them to conduct a sacrifice for Trisanku, and pronounces
a curse on those who decline to come

13f62785-a767-4c28-b09e-6fc831d512d0.canto_summary:
At the instance of Viswamitra the sages assembled at his hermitage
commence a sacrifice; on the gods failing to appear at the
sacrifice to accept the offerings, Viswamitra sends
TriSanku bodily to heaven by dint of his own
spiritual power, but the latter is expelled by
Indra, on which Viswamitra stops him in
the air and proceeds to create a new
heaven and desists from his purpose
only on the gods granting his desire

b31176fb-2354-454e-826c-e367ef50d1e7.canto_summary:
At the instance of Viswamitra the sages assembled at his hermitage
commence a sacrifice; on the gods failing to appear at the
sacrifice to accept the offerings, Viswamitra sends
TriSanku bodily to heaven by dint of his own
spiritual power, but the latter is expelled by
Indra, on which Viswamitra stops him in
the air and proceeds to create a new
heaven and desists from his purpose
only on the gods granting his desire

23864a62-5e53-4e0c-9a13-7ccbac34c9e7.canto_summary:
The animal to be sacrificed at the sacrificial performance of King Ambarisa
having been stolen away by Indra appearing in disguise, the arch-priest
enjoined the king to secure a human beast as a substitute. Wandering

in search of such a beast, Ambarisa saw the sage Rcika at
Bhrgutunga and requested him to hand over his juvenile
son in exchange for a hundred thousand cows. On the
parents declining to part with their eldest and youngest
sons, the middle one, Sunahsepa by name, voluntarily
offered himself for being sold and the king
returned with him to his capital

6ee2bad4-2569-4017-b16c-01868251feb4.canto_summary:
The animal to be sacrificed at the sacrificial performance of King Ambarisa
having been stolen away by Indra appearing in disguise, the arch-priest
enjoined the king to secure a human beast as a substitute. Wandering

in search of such a beast, Ambarisa saw the sage Rcika at
Bhrgutunga and requested him to hand over his juvenile
son in exchange for a hundred thousand cows. On the
parents declining to part with their eldest and youngest
sons, the middle one, Sunahsepa by name, voluntarily
offered himself for being sold and the king
returned with him to his capital

6427c84d-bac3-483e-8cec-d10f63084ce1.canto_summary:
On reaching Puskara, while Ambarisa is taking rest, Sunahsepa approaches
Viswamitra, who was practising austerities there, and inquires of him
a means of escaping death without meeting with the king’s
opposition, whereupon Viswamitra teaches him a prayer
each for propitiating Indra and Lord Visnu, respectively,
by reciting which the boy secures release from
Ambarisa’s bondage and the latter gets the
reward of the sacrifice without
sacrificing him

5842b72c-0fbd-4f94-a412-cdbe8c892722.canto_summary:
On reaching Puskara, while Ambarisa is taking rest, Sunahsepa approaches
Viswamitra, who was practising austerities there, and inquires of him
a means of escaping death without meeting with the king’s
opposition, whereupon Viswamitra teaches him a prayer
each for propitiating Indra and Lord Visnu, respectively,
by reciting which the boy secures release from
Ambarisa’s bondage and the latter gets the
reward of the sacrifice without
sacrificing him

fbb31993-fca2-402f-931d-7e7f0cd38033.canto_summary:
Brahma pays a visit to Viswamitra at Puskara and rewards him with
the status of a Rsi (seer). There he feels enamoured of Menaka,
a celestial nymph deputed by Indra, and enjoys life with
her for ten years. At last he realizes his folly and
retires to the Himalayas, where he renews his
austerities and is rewarded with the status of
a Maharsi by Brahma. Still dissatisfied,
he prosecutes his austerities with
renewed vigour

5673aa96-afba-4320-82aa-88606f334f95.canto_summary:
Brahma pays a visit to Viswamitra at Puskara and rewards him with
the status of a Rsi (seer). There he feels enamoured of Menaka,

her for ten years. At last he realizes his folly and
retires to the Himalayas, where he renews his
austerities and is rewarded with the status of
a Maharsi by Brahma. Still dissatisfied,
he prosecutes his austerities with
renewed vigour

05202d95-8b91-488a-bb4f-c233531e8323.canto_summary:
Petrifying by means of a curse Rambha, the celestial nymph
sent by Indra to wean him from his austerities,

Viswamitra resolves upon a further
course of austerities

b7185238-ca84-4ff3-8b6a-558236e01727.canto_summary:
Petrifying by means of a curse Rambha, the celestial nymph
sent by Indra to wean him from his austerities,

Viswamitra resolves upon a further
course of austerities

d66ee658-1095-4f4d-bb36-6e3cb0fcd70c.canto_summary:
On Viswamitra not ceasing from his austerities even on his being
conferred the title of a Brahmarsi by Brahma, Vasistha, as
urged by gods, recognizes it and here ends the narration

of Satananda. Having worshipped Vigwamitra,
King Janaka then returns to his palace

9d1e5576-ea32-4e4f-9337-573f883c85ea.canto_summary:
On Viswamitra not ceasing from his austerities even on his being

dba10a1e-4934-41fd-9b12-16e54cb83ad7.canto_summary:
On Viswamitra apprising Janaka of the eagerness of Sri Rama and
Laksmana to see his famous bow, Janaka reveals to him its

glory and tells him how he got it as well as Sita and
also of his pledge to give her in marriage to

Sri Rama if he

ce39f7a6-34b3-4ffe-9656-f12ddf86eade.canto_summary:
On Viswamitra apprising Janaka of the eagerness of Sri Rama and
Laksmana to see his famous bow, Janaka reveals to him its

glory and tells him how he got it as well as Sita and
also of his pledge to give her in marriage to

Sri Rama if he

a37defe1-aa00-48e0-8c1c-57695e67a226.canto_summary:
Urged by Viswamitra, Sri Rama bends the bow, sent by Janaka to
the sacrificial hall, in order to string it and in the process
breaks it, whereupon Janaka with the concurrence of
VisSwamitra sends his counsellors to Ayodhya
to invite Emperor Dasaratha for the wedding

e3083c82-e8ae-403c-9e28-d268da43a6ea.canto_summary:
Urged by Viswamitra, Sri Rama bends the bow, sent by Janaka to
the sacrificial hall, in order to string it and in the process
breaks it, whereupon Janaka with the concurrence of
VisSwamitra sends his counsellors to Ayodhya
to invite Emperor Dasaratha for the wedding

16849714-8d2c-4319-b46a-748b010cd51c.canto_summary:
Reaching Ayodhya, the counsellors of Janaka tell Dasaratha how Sri Rama
broke the bow of Lord Siva in Janaka’s custody and won the hand of
his daughter, and convey to him their master’s invitation for the
wedding, on which Dasaratha makes up his mind in consultation
with Vasistha to depart for Mithila at an early date

2e54450b-3db1-4d25-a7bb-0e692b7b067d.canto_summary:
With a large number of followers, DaSaratha proceeds to Mithila for the
wedding and is received with signal honour by Janaka and his
people and comfortably lodged

94883684-8d54-48cc-b0e7-1723e0010cec.canto_summary:
Janaka sends for his younger brother, KuSadhwaja, from Sankasya.
Invited by him, DaSaratha meets Janaka at the latter’s palace,
where at the instance of DaSaratha, Vasistha glorifies
the race of Ikswaku

ae97ea4b-a586-45e7-a7cf-04fa484d8615.canto_summary:
Janaka sends for his younger brother, KuSadhwaja, from Sankasya.
Invited by him, DaSaratha meets Janaka at the latter’s palace,
where at the instance of DaSaratha, Vasistha glorifies
the race of Ikswaku

5b21569e-df1b-4951-aea4-6dc28e5163e8.canto_summary:
Janaka sends for his younger brother, KuSadhwaja, from Sankasya.
Invited by him, DaSaratha meets Janaka at the latter’s palace,
where at the instance of DaSaratha, Vasistha glorifies
the race of Ikswaku

eae57087-ca11-4296-b639-c6f15a84df5e.canto_summary:
Recounting his own pedigree, Janaka offers the hand of his
two daughters, Sita and Urmila, to Sri Rama
and Laksmana, respectively

f6fd166f-fb6a-49fd-82b7-d7b5f9cdd077.canto_summary:
Recounting his own pedigree, Janaka offers the hand of his
two daughters, Sita and Urmila, to Sri Rama
and Laksmana, respectively

3291957d-3eb8-4f56-9792-1f8c90f8eff9.canto_summary:
Vasistha and ViSwamitra jointly ask for the hand of the two daughters
of Kusgadhwaja in favour of Bharata and Satrughna and Janaka
acquiesces in the proposal. Thereupon DaSaratha gets his
sons to perform the rite of Samavartana and himself
performs the Nandisraddha

ddd8a64e-09a2-4a22-96a0-d7ce6b332830.canto_summary:
Vasistha and ViSwamitra jointly ask for the hand of the two daughters
of Kusgadhwaja in favour of Bharata and Satrughna and Janaka
acquiesces in the proposal. Thereupon DaSaratha gets his
sons to perform the rite of Samavartana and himself
performs the Nandisraddha

49bf70e7-bc0f-4f45-b685-7ffa9470ad57.canto_summary:
Janaka escorts DaSaratha and his four sons clad in nuptial attire to the pavilion
erected for the wedding. Placing Vigwamitra and Satananda ahead,
Vasistha conducts the marriage ceremony. Sri Rama and his three

brothers clasp the hand of Sita and her sisters. Singing and
dancing for joy, the gods rain heavenly flowers
on the brides and bridegrooms

f45e072d-7507-45a1-987d-1112186dd861.canto_summary:
Janaka escorts DaSaratha and his four sons clad in nuptial attire to the pavilion
erected for the wedding. Placing Vigwamitra and Satananda ahead,
Vasistha conducts the marriage ceremony. Sri Rama and his three

brothers clasp the hand of Sita and her sisters. Singing and
dancing for joy, the gods rain heavenly flowers
on the brides and bridegrooms

06b5431a-52df-434a-9861-48985f0bb342.canto_summary:
Janaka escorts DaSaratha and his four sons clad in nuptial attire to the pavilion
erected for the wedding. Placing Vigwamitra and Satananda ahead,
Vasistha conducts the marriage ceremony. Sri Rama and his three

brothers clasp the hand of Sita and her sisters. Singing and
dancing for joy, the gods rain heavenly flowers
on the brides and bridegrooms

406726e0-394e-4e43-a360-feb22ca0e3d7.canto_summary:
Taking leave of Janaka and DaSaratha, Viswamitra returns to his own
hermitage and, accepting large wedding presents, DaSaratha too
turns back to Ayodhya alongwith his sons and their newly-
wedded brides. On the way the irascible and redoubtable
Parasurama, a sworn enemy of the Ksatriyas, suddenly
appears before them, axe in hand, and Vasistha
and the other sages accompanying the
party offer worship to him

1ec05495-dc2e-477b-a01f-e4575333566a.canto_summary:
Taking leave of Janaka and DaSaratha, Viswamitra returns to his own
hermitage and, accepting large wedding presents, DaSaratha too
turns back to Ayodhya alongwith his sons and their newly-
wedded brides. On the way the irascible and redoubtable
Parasurama, a sworn enemy of the Ksatriyas, suddenly
appears before them, axe in hand, and Vasistha
and the other sages accompanying the
party offer worship to him

a2d9f6f2-3ec0-4667-8bfe-6c6ac4afa1b1.canto_summary:
Turning a deaf ear to DaSaratha’s prayer, ParaSurama relates the
history of the bows belonging to Lords Siva and Visnu
and challenges Sri Rama to string the bow of
Lord Visnu in his possession

733d3008-a028-4e94-97ba-5445a264ddd3.canto_summary:
Turning a deaf ear to DaSaratha’s prayer, ParaSurama relates the
history of the bows belonging to Lords Siva and Visnu
and challenges Sri Rama to string the bow of
Lord Visnu in his possession

156992d0-f104-484d-aa0b-052f2b50a104.canto_summary:
Fitting the arrow to the bow of Lord Visnu and declaring it as unfailing,
Sri Rama asks Parasurama to point out at whom it may be
discharged, and at the instance of the latter puts an
end to his title to the (ethereal) worlds earned
by him through his austerities. Recognizing
Sri Rama to be no other than Lord Visnu
and taking leave of him, ParaSurama
withdraws to Mount Mahendra
in order to resume
his austerities

8b0c05a6-fc30-44da-a33b-9eb0cc8d472b.canto_summary:
Fitting the arrow to the bow of Lord Visnu and declaring it as unfailing,
Sri Rama asks Parasurama to point out at whom it may be
discharged, and at the instance of the latter puts an
end to his title to the (ethereal) worlds earned
by him through his austerities. Recognizing
Sri Rama to be no other than Lord Visnu
and taking leave of him, ParaSurama
withdraws to Mount Mahendra
in order to resume
his austerities

9825577f-da6a-43b6-8d4c-45fd06af0985.canto_summary:
On the departure of Paragurama, Sri Rama hands over the bow of Lord Visnu
to Varuna (the god of water) and, sending his army ahead, King Dasaratha
enters Ayodhya. After some days Prince Yudhajit, Bharata’s maternal
uncle takes away Bharata and Satrughna to his father’s capital

dc63fa1e-0a28-4db5-817f-d1e9f89d36ba.canto_summary:
